title: Interactive Shell Capability — Stateful Execution with Brokered Command Authorization
description: Extends the CapabilityBroker to authorize and manage stateful interactive shell sessions (SSH, reverse shells, pseudo-TTYs). Introduces dual-gate authorization (session + per-command), command filtering pipeline, and TTY output ingestion into EvidenceGraph/WorldModel.

required: D-Series (Cognitive Architecture): Arena, Planner, CapabilityBroker, SafetyVerifier, Evaluator, WorldModel, EvidenceGraph
forbidden_modifications: CapabilityBroker public interface (only extension via register_capability)

architecture.overview: Interactive shells are stateful, long-lived capabilities. Unlike stateless probes (HTTP, banner grabs), a shell session maintains a persistent connection with bidirectional I/O. The architecture introduces: (1) InteractiveShellCapability — wrapper around pwntools/paramiko/sshlib; (2) ShellSession — brokered state object tracked by CapabilityBroker; (3) CommandFilterPipeline — static allowlist + LLM intent classifier; (4) TTYNormalizer — converts raw ANSI/terminal output to structured Evidence.

interface.connect: Establish connection (SSH, reverse shell, bind shell, meterpreter). Returns ShellSession.
interface.send_command: Send a single command string; returns raw output (stdout+stderr) and exit code.
interface.send_raw: Send raw bytes (for interactive prompts, Ctrl-C, etc.).

components.name: ShellSession
lifecycle: PROPOSED → Planner proposes session via Candidate(action_type='shell_connect', ...)
AUTHORIZED → Broker.authorize_shell_session() returns SessionReceipt with session_id, allowed_targets, max_duration, max_idle, allowed_commands_pattern
CONNECTING → Capability.connect() called; on success → ACTIVE
ACTIVE → Commands flow through Broker.authorize_shell_command() per-command
IDLE → No commands for max_idle seconds; Broker may auto-terminate
TERMINATING → Broker revokes or timeout reached; Capability.close() called
TERMINATED → Final state; session archived in EvidenceGraph

fields.status: enum[PROPOSED, AUTHORIZED, CONNECTING, ACTIVE, IDLE, TERMINATING, TERMINATED, ERROR]

components.name: CommandFilterPipeline
components.description: Two-tier filter applied to every command proposed during an ACTIVE ShellSession.

tier_1_static_allowlist.description: Regex pattern match against ShellSession.allowed_commands_pattern. Fast, deterministic, no LLM.

tier_2_llm_intent_classifier.description: Commands not matching allowlist or explicitly denied are escalated to LLM classifier.
tier_2_llm_intent_classifier.classifier_prompt: You are a security policy classifier for an autonomous penetration testing agent. Classify the proposed shell command as one of: ALLOW (read-only enumeration, safe), ESCALATE (requires Planner falsification step), DENY (destructive, lateral movement, persistence, data exfiltration, privilege escalation beyond scope). Command: '{command}'. Context: Target={target}, Session={session_id}, User={username}, WorkingDir={cwd}. Respond with JSON: {"decision": "ALLOW|ESCALATE|DENY", "reason": "...", "risk_level": "LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH|CRITICAL"}.

decisions.ESCALATE: Pause command; create FalsificationTask for Planner; resume only if Planner confirms with evidence
decisions.DENY: Reject command; increment denied_command_count; if > 3 in 60s → auto-terminate session

components.name: TTYNormalizer
components.description: Converts raw ANSI/terminal byte streams into structured Evidence for EvidenceGraph and WorldModel.
pipeline: Strip ANSI escape sequences (colors, cursor movement, OSC)
Detect prompt (regex: PS1 patterns, $/#/>) to segment command/response
Parse structured output: JSON, XML, CSV, key=value, table formats
Extract observables: file paths, IPs, users, processes, ports, hashes, credentials
Emit Evidence objects with type: COMMAND_OUTPUT, FILE_CONTENT, PROCESS_LIST, NETWORK_CONNECTIONS, USER_ACCOUNTS, CREDENTIAL, VULNERABILITY_INDICATOR

new_methods.name: authorize_shell_session
new_methods.description: Validates session proposal against scope, creates ShellSession in AUTHORIZED state, provisions listener if reverse shell.
validation: LHOST/LPORT in authorized egress range (for reverse shells)
Allowed commands pattern is safe regex (no ReDoS)
new_methods.returns: SessionReceipt { session_id, authorized: true, expires_at, restrictions: { allowed_commands_pattern, max_idle, heartbeat_interval }, listener_info?: { lhost, lport, protocol } }

new_methods.name: authorize_shell_command
new_methods.signature: authorize_shell_command(session_id: str, command: str, context: dict) -> CommandReceipt
validation: Command fails Tier 1 → Tier 2 LLM classifier
Tier 2 ESCALATE → create FalsificationTask, return PENDING_FALSIFICATION
Tier 2 DENY → reject, increment denied counter, check auto-terminate threshold
new_methods.returns: CommandReceipt { authorized: bool, decision: ALLOW|ESCALATE|DENY, reason, falsification_task_id?, session_status }

new_methods.name: terminate_shell_session
new_methods.description: Force-closes session. Called by Broker (timeout, policy violation) or Planner (objective complete).

falsification_tasks.description: Planner must prove command is safe and necessary for current objective. Evidence required: expected output pattern, risk mitigation, rollback plan.

fields: processes: list[{pid, ppid, user, cmd, cpu, mem}]
connections: list[{proto, local_addr, remote_addr, state, pid}]
accounts: list[{username, uid, gid, home, shell, groups}]

evidence_ingestion.worldmodel_updates: Each Evidence → WorldModel.update_host_state(target, evidence) → updates HostState.{files, processes, network, users, credentials, vulns}

listener_management.provisioned_by: CapabilityBroker only (never Planner or Capability directly)
listener_management.listener_lifecycle: Created on authorize_shell_session (reverse_tcp); destroyed on terminate_shell_session

callback_validation.on_connect: Verify source IP in authorized scope; verify destination port matches authorized listener
callback_validation.on_command: Verify session_id matches active session; verify command authorized

safety_invariants: INV-E1-01: No shell session exists without a valid SessionReceipt from CapabilityBroker.
INV-E1-02: No command executes in a shell session without a CommandReceipt (ALLOW or ESCALATE+PASS).
INV-E1-03: Reverse shell listeners only bind to authorized LHOST/LPORT provisioned by Broker.
INV-E1-04: Shell sessions cannot exceed max_duration; auto-terminate on expiry.
INV-E1-05: Idle sessions auto-terminate after max_idle seconds.
INV-E1-06: Denied command threshold (default 3 in 60s) triggers session termination.
INV-E1-07: All TTY output normalized to Evidence within 5 seconds of receipt.
INV-E1-08: ShellSession state persisted to SQLite (sessions.db) for crash recovery.
INV-E1-09: CapabilityBroker holds exclusive kill-switch; no component can bypass terminate_shell_session().

configuration.overrides: Per-session overrides allowed via ShellSessionProposal fields; validated by Broker against policy maximums.

unit: CommandFilterPipeline: allowlist matches, denies, LLM classifier mock
TTYNormalizer: ANSI strip, backspace, prompt detection, JSON/table parsing
integration: Broker.authorize_shell_command: DENY → counter increment → threshold → terminate
Crash recovery: sessions.db persists, sessions resume or clean up on restart
adversarial: Command injection in proposed command (semicolon, backtick, $(), &&, ||)
ANSI escape sequence injection in output
Prompt spoofing (fake PS1 to confuse normalizer)
Reverse shell callback from unauthorized IP
LLM classifier prompt injection via command string

rollback_plan: If E1 causes instability: CapabilityBroker.unregister_capability('interactive_shell'); terminate all active sessions; disable shell_* candidate types in Planner.
seal_criteria: All safety invariants have corresponding implementation tests
Egress control listener CIDR/port ranges configured for deployment environment
